newsitem.title: USA: High-yield emerging market debt perks up.
newsitem.headline: High-yield emerging market debt perks up.

text.p: High yielding emerging market bonds, taking advantage of the steady tone in U.S. Treasuries, rose smartly in moderate trading on Thursday, traders and analysts said.
Bulgaria and Ecuador debts were the leading gainers, while others moved up mainly in line with U.S. Treasuries, they said.
The sentiment has improved greatly since the low U.S. inflation numbers in March consumer price index released on Tuesday lifted the mood in the Treasuries, a trader said.
"We expect the market to do well in the next two weeks," he said, noting that no significant U.S. data release is expected before May to spoil the mood.
Ecuador's Brady bonds climbed, even though its eurobond launch was still in limbo, analysts said.

Source closed to the deal told Reuters that the two-part offering, comprising a five-year fixed and a seven-year floating, would total $300 million to $400 million. The launch was delayed apparently as issuers bowed to the unfavorable market conditions.
Analysts, however, were skeptical that the size would be increased to $400 million, since demand for the initially planned $300 million failed to generate enough interest.
Ecuador was able to postpone the launch because of a grace period for repaying the $300 million bridge loan due April 9, said an analyst who requested anonymity.
Price talk for the five-year fixed rate note hovered around 475 to 500 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, with some speculating on an even wider spread.
Ecuador IEB, which matures on December 21, 2004, would have served as a handy reference, but traders preferred comparison with the longer and more liquid PDI with maturity on Februry 28, 2015.
Ecuador PDI rose 1-3/8 to 57.00 bid, while IEB eased 1/8 to 83-1/2 bid.
"Even with today's rally, PDI still trades some 760 basis points (over U.S. Treasury)," said a trader. "475 to 500 for five-year could be a hard sell."
Ecuador needs a standby loan from the IMF before proceeding to renegotiate its Paris Club debt. An IMF mission is currently in Quito reviewing the fiscal situation.

President Fabian Alarcom presented a "credible" austerity fiscal package on February 28 to reduce the fiscal deficit to 2.5 percent of the gross domestic product, but since then he backpedalled on some planned price hikes to avoid hurting his precarious popularity, said another analyst.
"The market has low expectation of what Alarcon could accomplish in his interim presidency," he noted.
Fabian Alarcon became caretaker president after Abdala Bucaram was ousted by parliament in early February. His mandate expires in May 1998.
Bulgaria Brady bonds powered ahead amid relief that the country's worst financialcrisis was over, traders said.
Bulgaria FLRB jumped 1-1/4 to 44-1/2 bid.
The country received on Thursday $178.7 million disbursement of the $657 million funding package approved by the International Monetary Fund last week.
Bulgarians will go to the polls on Saturday in parliamentary elections that would put market reformers to power. Early elections were called after popular protests toppled the Socialists in February.
(( -- Nailene Chou Wiest - 212-859-1674))
